claims.text: Reducing FeMnNiGeSi-type high-entropy alloys to nanoscale films or nanoribbons suppresses long-range magnetic-domain coherence.
Suppressed magnetic-domain coherence reduces the magnetocaloric response.
Suppressed magnetic-domain coherence increases hysteresis during low-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
As-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type nanofilms and patterned nanoribbons contain microstructural defects and strain and are affected by edges.
Magnetic-field-assisted post-deposition annealing relaxes interfacial strain and defects.
Magnetic-field-assisted annealing encourages magnetic-domain alignment and partially restores domain connectivity.
Magnetic-domain size and connectivity are modulated by interfacial strain, grain-boundary relaxation, and defect density.
Dimensional confinement increases the relative importance of interfacial and edge effects.
Interfacial and edge effects disrupt coherent magnetic ordering in confined FeMnNiGeSi-type alloys.
Nanoscale defects and interfaces promote domain-wall pinning.
Domain-wall pinning produces higher magnetic hysteresis in the as-deposited samples.
Annealing-induced local reordering and strain relaxation recover magnetic-domain coherence.
Relative to the as-deposited baseline, annealed samples will show an enhanced magnetocaloric effect.
The enhanced magnetocaloric effect will be observable as an increase in adiabatic temperature change.
Relative to the as-deposited baseline, annealed samples will show reduced magnetic hysteresis.
Reduced hysteresis will be observable as a narrowing of the magnetic coercivity loop.
The proposed mechanism applies near the alloy's magnetocaloric transition and at dimensions where surface and interface effects are significant relative to bulk behavior.
Heat-transfer rates limit the usable magnetic-cooling cycle frequency.
